slides.title: Culinary Crossovers
slides.text: Spices tie the two cuisines together. Tunisian cooking is built on caraway, coriander, cumin, cinnamon and chilli, with harissa on the table; Bahraini cooking uses cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, turmeric and saffron, with mahyawa fish sauce. Both love grains: couscous in Tunisia, rice (machboos) and cracked wheat (harees) in Bahrain. Both celebrate with a whole roasted lamb: mechoui in Tunisia and quzi in Bahrain. Both start the day with egg: Tunisian ojja and Bahraini balaleet.
